newsitem.title: USA: JP Foodservice to buy Rykoff for $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: JP Foodservice to buy Rykoff for $1.4 billion.

text.p: JP Foodservice Inc. has agreed to acquire Rykoff-Sexton Inc. in a deal worth $1.4 billion in cash and debt, creating a food-service giant with annual sales of $5.2 billion, the companies said on Monday.
Together, the companies will have nationwide distribution capabilities and a customer base of more than 130,000 hotel, restaurant and institutional food-service customers.
They will hold 4 percent of the $140 billion industry, the companies said -- still a far second to industry giant Sysco Corp.'s 10 percent.

"The merger of the No. 3 player (Rykoff-Sexton) and the No. 5 player (JP) will create a strong No. 2 broad-line food service distributor with a complete national presence," Morgan Stanley Dean Witter analyst John Renwick said in a research note.

Rykoff shareholders will receive 0.84 JP share for each Rykoff share in a tax-free transaction. The exchange ratio will not change if JP's stock price changes, the companies said in a news release. It is expected that JP and Rykoff shareholders will own equal stakes in the combined company.
JP and Rykoff stock did not trade early Monday. JP stock later fell $1.44 to $28.69 and Rykoff rose $3.69 to $23.31, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal, in which JP will assume $700 million of Rykoff debt, is expected to add to JP's earnings in 1998 and thereafter, the companies said.
The headquarters of the new company will be in Columbia, Md., the current home of JP. Rykoff is based in Wilkes-Barre, Pa.

JP Chairman and Chief Executive Jim Miller will be chairman and chief executive of the new company, while Rykoff Chairman and Chief Executive Mark Van Stekelenburg will be vice chairman and president. The merged companies will be called JP Foodservice Inc; its operating units will do business as US Foodservice.
Spokesmen for the companies were not available to comment on possible layoffs or consolidations due to the merger.

Miller said in an interview after the deal was announced that the food service industry "is about 15 years behind the retail (food) industry when regional chains like Safeway bought up ma-and-pa grocieries."

Analyst Ken Shea of Standard & Poor's, said, "I am surprised (a large merger in the industry) has taken so long. Sysco is the leader in an extremely fragmented market, so it does not surprise me there is a consolidation wave. JP and Rykoff are near the top of the industry, but will not dent Sysco because it is so large."
The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.
